content: In a trachoma-endemic region of southern Mexico, neonatal conjunctivitis has been studied, with findings published in the British Journal of Ophthalmology. Research has explored the use of neonatal ocular prophylaxis to prevent chlamydial and gonococcal conjunctivitis. Zanoni, Isenberg, and Apt conducted a comparative study of silver nitrate versus erythromycin for the prevention of ophthalmia neonatorum, with results published in Clinical Pediatrics. Hedberg and colleagues reported an outbreak of erythromycin-resistant staphylococcal conjunctivitis in a newborn nursery, as documented in Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal. Isenberg, Apt, and Wood performed a controlled trial evaluating povidone-iodine as a prophylactic agent against ophthalmia neonatorum, with findings published in the New England Journal of Medicine. Ison and collaborators examined the prevalence and distribution of Neisseria gonorrhoeae strains in the United States that exhibit plasmid-mediated, high-level resistance to tetracycline, with their work appearing in the Journal of Infectious Diseases. Schwarcz, Zenilman, Schnell, and others analyzed the cost-effectiveness of community-based interventions aimed at reducing the prevalence of chlamydia in Sweden, as reported in Scandinavian Journal of Public Health. Keenan, Eckert, and Rutar conducted a cost analysis of povidone-iodine for ophthalmia neonatorum prophylaxis, with their findings published in Archives of Ophthalmology. McDonald and colleagues reviewed the efficacy of various ocular prophylactic agents used to prevent gonococcal and chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum, as detailed in the Journal of Midwifery & Women’s Health. Lastly, Kakar, Bhalla, Maria, Rana, Chawla, and Mathur contributed to the body of research on neonatal conjunctivitis and its prevention.
